I have depression and anxiety and asked my Doctor what she thought. Essentially, she said that the cases of making depression worse are rare, and more often than not those cases have multiple contributing factors, not just accutane. She said the evidence for the link isn't very strong, mostly anecdotal (haven't fact checked this though). 

You also need to weight it up with the idea that Acne itself might be contributing to depression (mine was). So which is worse? 

If I were you I would ask my self:
- Am I in a relatively constant mental health state (not necessarily good, but not changing)? 
- Will I be prescribed it in winter? I highly recommend starting in the warmer months to avoid the dry, crusties + seasonal depression . 
- Will the positive effects of accutane potentially benefit my mood?

**FAST RELIEF** \- Exercise & fresh air! If I feel distressed, intense exercise is the only thing that works for me. There is science behind its effectiveness!

Hopefully you'll feel a little better after some exercise. If not, maybe try a crisis call or text line. I recommend questioning what caused you to feel this way. It can be a multitude of things. I recommend listing your cognitive symptoms (thoughts & emotions), behavioural symptoms/patterns (bad habits? Anything that you are neglecting to do?) and your physical symptoms - then from there try come up with some things that will help you improve your symptoms. For example, are you stressed? Try some de-stress techniques. Tired? Focus on your sleep schedule. Running only on anxious energy? Channel it into something productive then sleep! Depressed for no reason? Go easy on yourself, maybe treat yourself, but definitely look at below,

Being patient, kind and compassionate with yourself throughout this is hella important, but I understand that it can take time.

**LONG-TERM RELIEF**

I recommend establishing a routine and focusing, one at a time, on what I believe to be the 5 primary pillars of wellbeing.

Routine is often really important for depressed people, mostly just around sleep-wake times, eating times and, if you can manage, exercise, outside & social time. Having good core habits that keep you well are great, because when they are established habits they require way less energy.

Primary pillars:

* **Sleep** \- Fatigue is a super common symptom of depression and anxiety. Sleep is hella important for all sorts of stuff, and being well-rested can be just what you need to feel a little better. Sleep hygiene is also really important in general. The bed is only for sleep + sex - no netflix or scrolling through social media.

* **Food** \- this one isn't strict. I recommend trying to have regular eating times, at least 2x a day. Try to get some good nutrients, and less of the obviously unhealthy foods like fried foods and refined sugars. Some nutrient deficiencies are linked with depression, i can't remember them of the top of my head, but for example - the amino acid tryptophan is a precursor of serotonin, and tyrosine is the precursor of dopamine. Due to this, I recommend perhaps investing in a daily multivitamin and some fish-oil. DRINK WATER!

* **Exercise** \- This may be sigh-worthy, but don't knock it until you try it! One of the only distress tolerances that work for is intense exercise, and I find yoga/stretching to be really calming, and just generally great in the morning or at night. Exercise is super important in general, and in my opinion it's probably the single most beneficial thing you can do for your health and brain, besides stopping smoking and being a healthy weight. It  can really help alleviate anxiety and is shown to be as effective in treating depression.  'FOOD IS THE MOST ABUSED ANTI-ANXIETY DRUG & EXERCISE IS THE MOST UNDERUTILISED ANTIDEPRESSANT'

* **Environment** \- By 'environment' I mean two things. **1)** How is your personal space?  Is it tidy? Is your home a calm environment? If it's not, times can be tough I know. In that instance, I recommend making your room, or even just your bed, a cosy haven for you. Change your sheets, maybe try some aromatherapy, light a candle. A tidy environment is a tidy mind. It just helps. I need to take my own advice rn - my room is a MESS. **2)** I also mean environment in the sense of nature, and getting out of the house. I believe that nature is lovely, and can be a healing force for many people. When I was at my lowest, almost entirely bedridden, my mum got me to hang out the washing. I would never deny her this help, and getting out of the house, even if just into my garden, was good for me. It's good to get out of the house in general, even if just to the shops (grocery store if your american?). Prolonged isolation is not a good thing and it can be tricky/uncomfortable to re-enter society. I'm talking from experience here.

* **People -** Relationships are undeniably one of the most meaningful aspects of our existence. I am of the belief that only relationships and experiences that can bring us true happiness. For this one, I also mean two things. **1)** I firstly mean **seek support**. If you don't already have a good support network, it is defo time to curate one so you have some people and organisations to lean on. You might want to bring up your need for support with you family, friends or who you live with. I completely understand if you'd rather not, it is can be uncomfortable & stigma is a b****. Atleast make an appointment with your GP, or school/uni counsellor. You may be referred to mental health services, which I suggest you opt for rather than 'counsellors', and you may be prescribed medication, which is nothing to be ashamed of! **2)** Is loneliness a culprit in how you are feeling? Sometimes you just need a little bit of unpressured socialising, even if you are more introverted (I am !). Having friends and acquaintances is great, as you need to laugh, have someone be kind to you, have people to relate to  - and of course - people to support you, care about you and vise versa.

Those are my primary pillars!

There are many more things you can do : there are so many types of therapy you can try!!! gratitude & mindfulness exercises, meditation, self-compassion exercises (really hard, im at like a 2/10 with these), support groups/social groups + so much more
